words.enExample: The smell of chalk evokes memories of my first classroom.
words.zhExample: 粉笔的气味唤起了我对第一间教室的记忆。
words.note: e-（出）+ voke（叫），把记忆/情感"叫出来"。注意与 invoke（援引、调用）区分：evoke 唤起情感，invoke 援引规则或力量。evoke memories / evoke sympathy 高频搭配。

words.meaning: 真诚的；真正的；名副其实的
words.enExample: What impressed the interviewers most was her genuine interest in the project.
words.zhExample: 最令面试官印象深刻的是她对项目真诚的兴趣。
words.note: 原义"天生的、纯种的"，引申为"非伪装的"。a genuine smile（发自内心的微笑）/ genuine leather（真皮）。近义 authentic / sincere。

words.meaning: 至关重要的；必要的； imperative：必要的事
words.enExample: It is imperative that we back up the data before migrating the system.
words.zhExample: 在系统迁移之前，我们必须备份数据，这一点至关重要。
words.note: It is imperative that + (should) do 虚拟语气，与 essential 同级但更正式。语法术语中 imperative 还指"祈使语气"。军事、商务文书高频词。

words.enExample: The guests lingered over coffee until midnight, unwilling to end the evening.
words.zhExample: 客人们喝着咖啡一直聊到深夜，不愿结束这个夜晚。
words.note: linger over something 慢慢品味、迟迟不结束；linger on 继续存在（The smell lingered on for days）。近义 stay / remain，但 linger 自带"舍不得走"的情绪色彩。

words.enExample: In the desert, water is scarce and every drop is carefully stored.
words.zhExample: 在沙漠里水极为稀缺，每一滴都被小心储存起来。
words.note: make oneself scarce（溜走、避开）是地道口语。名词 scarcity（稀缺性，经济学高频词）。近义 rare，但 rare 强调"罕见"，scarce 强调"不够用"。

essay.title: A Letter to My Younger Self
essay.author: 佚名
paragraphs: Dear younger me, I write to you from a future you cannot imagine and will not believe: you are, at last, mostly fine. I know you keep a list of your failures in a notebook nobody will ever read. Burn it. None of the entries turned out to be permanent.

That thing you are afraid will define you — the failed exam, the friendship that dissolved, the summer you wasted — will instead become a story you tell at dinner, softer and funnier each year. Pain does not last; only our retelling of it does, and we control the retelling.

Two warnings. First, the people you are trying so hard to impress are not watching; they are busy worrying about their own performance. Second, the things you postpone out of fear — the conversation, the trip, the apology — grow heavier with waiting, never lighter. Almost everything is easier today than it will be in five years.

And one comfort: you will not become the person you are planning to be. You will become someone stranger, kinder, and more specific — shaped by books you have not yet heard of and losses you cannot foresee. That is not a plan failing. That is a life happening. With more tenderness than you expect, — yourself, later.
translations: 亲爱的年少的我：我从一个你无法想象也不会相信的未来写信给你——你终于基本安好。我知道你在一本永远无人翻看的笔记本里记录着自己的失败。烧掉它吧。那些条目，没有一条最终成为定局。
那件你害怕将定义你一生的事——失手的考试、无疾而终的友谊、荒废的夏天——终会成为你在餐桌上讲述的故事，而且一年比一年温柔、好笑。痛苦不会长存；长存的只是我们对它的复述，而复述的方式由我们掌握。
给你两个提醒。第一，你拼命想留下好印象的那些人，其实并没有在看你，他们都忙着担忧自己的表现。第二，你因恐惧而推迟的事——那次谈话、那趟旅行、那句道歉——只会越等越重，不会越等越轻。几乎所有事，今天做都比五年后做容易。
还有一句安慰：你不会成为计划中的那个人。你会成为一个更奇特、更善良也更具体的人——由你尚未听说过的书和你无法预见的失去塑造而成。这不是计划的失败，这是生活的发生。带着比你预想更多的温柔——后来的你。

grammar.point: I write to you from... — 现在时表当前动作
grammar.example: "I write to you from a future you cannot imagine and will not believe."
grammar.note: 一般现在时 write 描绘写信当下；you cannot imagine 和 (that) you will not believe 为并列定语从句修饰 a future。 举一反三：I speak to you from a place you will reach one day.

grammar.point: None of the entries turned out to be... — turn out 结构
grammar.example: "None of the entries turned out to be permanent."
grammar.note: turn out to be + 形容词/名词表示“结果是、最终成为”，强调与预期不同的结局。none of + 复数名词作主语时谓语可用单数或复数。 举一反三：The hardest year turned out to be the most useful one.

grammar.point: shaped by...and... — 过去分词短语作后置定语
grammar.example: "You will become someone stranger, kinder, and more specific — shaped by books you have not yet heard of."
grammar.note: shaped by... 修饰 someone，相当于 who is shaped by...；hear of 听说，用于否定完成时 you have not yet heard of。 举一反三：She arrived as a stranger — shaped by cities she had never named.

vocab.enExample: No mistake at seventeen is permanent.
vocab.zhExample: 十七岁时的错误没有一个是永久的。
vocab.note: 用法：permanent record 永久记录；反义 temporary

vocab.enExample: One failure does not define a person.
vocab.zhExample: 一次失败不能定义一个人。
vocab.note: 用法：define someone 以某事定义某人

vocab.zhExample: 这段合伙关系无声无息地解体了。
vocab.note: 用法：友谊、合伙等的“瓦解”常用 dissolve

vocab.enExample: Healing often begins with a gentler retelling.
vocab.zhExample: 治愈常始于一次更温柔的复述。

vocab.enExample: She postponed the conversation for two winters.
vocab.zhExample: 那场对话，她拖了两个冬天。
vocab.note: 用法：postpone doing something 接动名词

vocab.enExample: Stop trying to impress an audience that is not there.
vocab.zhExample: 别再试图取悦一群并不存在的观众。

vocab.enExample: No one can foresee which friendship will save them.
vocab.zhExample: 没有人能预见哪段友情终将拯救自己。

vocab.enExample: The letter ended with unexpected tenderness.
vocab.zhExample: 信在一种出乎意料的温柔中结束。
vocab.note: 用法：形容词 tender，比 kindness 更细腻
